questions.question: What is the difference between include and extend in Ruby?
questions.title: Include vs Extend
questions.direct_answer: `include` adds a module's methods as INSTANCE methods; `extend` adds them as CLASS (singleton) methods. class C; include M; end -> C.new has M's methods (instance). class C; extend M; end -> C itself has M's methods (class methods, called C.method). You can also extend a single object: obj.extend(M) -> only that object gets M's methods (no others). include is for sharing behavior across instances (a mixin); extend is for adding class-level helpers or one-off object behavior. A common pattern: module M; def self.included(base); base.extend(ClassMethods); end; module ClassMethods; ...; end — gives both instance and class methods when included. Use include when instances need the methods; extend when the class (or one object) needs them.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using include when you wanted class methods (use extend), or expecting extend to affect instances.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: include = instance methods (C.new has them); extend = class/singleton methods (C has them, or one obj). include for mixins; extend for class helpers.

```ruby
  def hello; 'hi from M'; end
end

# include -> INSTANCE methods

  include Greet
end
A.new.hello      # 'hi from M'  (instance method)
# A.hello        # NoMethodError (not a class method)

# extend -> CLASS (singleton) methods
class B
  extend Greet
end
B.hello         # 'hi from M'   (class method)
# B.new.hello    # NoMethodError (not an instance method)

# extend a SINGLE object (only that object gets the methods)
c = Object.new
c.extend(Greet)
c.hello         # 'hi from M'  (only c, not other Objects)

# The classic pattern: include gives instance + class methods
class C
  include Greet          # instance methods
  extend Greet           # also class methods (independent)
end

# included hook pattern (gives both when you `include`):
module Mixin
  def self.included(base)
    base.extend(ClassMethods)
  end
  def instance_m; 'inst'; end
  module ClassMethods
    def class_m; 'cls'; end
  end
end
class D; include Mixin; end
D.new.instance_m   # 'inst'
D.class_m          # 'cls'

# include = instances; extend = class or one object.
```
